text:
Carla (customer): Hey team — our private deployment (org-42, eu-west-1) just started failing about 10m ago. Model inference calls are returning 502 / TLS handshake timeout. Can you check the VPC peering / VPN side? :sadpanda:

Alice (support): Sorry you're hitting this — we're on it. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (cert rotate, firewall rules, routing)?

Carla (customer): No infra changes on our side. We did have a cert rotate scheduled earlier but it completed without errors. All nodes in the VPC show healthy. Logs show TLS handshake error between control-plane proxy and private-serving host.

Alice (support): Thanks. Ben / Dave, can you look at the IPsec/S2S tunnel state for org-42? Sounds like tunnel might be up but encrypted traffic failing.

Ben (netops): Looking. Initial check: the tunnel is ESTABLISHED on our side but IKEv2 rekey logs show repeated CHILD_SA rejections. Could be a proposal mismatch after rekey.

Dave (eng-runtime): We saw TLS timeouts in the runtime logs too. Correlating: every failed inference corresponds to a phase2 rekey around the same timestamp. Sending recent logs.

Alice (support): Carla, can you run a quick curl from an app pod to the private-serving IP and paste the error?

Carla (customer): Curl output:
```
$ curl -v https://10.200.8.12:443/health
* Trying 10.200.8.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.200.8.12 (10.200.8.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) TLS handshake timeout
```

Ben (netops): Ok that matches. On our IPsec gateway:
```
# sudo ipsec statusall | grep org-42
org-42: INSTALLED, TUNNEL, reqid 12345, ESPinUDP4, 10.200.8.0/24 <==> 10.0.32.0/24
  installed: esp=aes_gcm16_256-ecp384,aead=1
  rekeying failed: CHILD_SA not acceptable (proposal)
```

Ben (netops): The rekey attempt shows the remote selected `aes_gcm8_128` while our RA offers `aes_gcm16_256`. Strange — we pin proposals in infra as part of security policy.

Dave (eng-runtime): We recently updated a kernel-level crypto policy on the private-serving hosts to prefer smaller GCM tags for latency, but that shouldn't change network-level SA proposals. Could the customer's gateway be cycling to an older policy?

Carla (customer): Our gateway is managed by a 3rd-party appliance (not ours). They pushed a micro-update ~15m before failures and said it was 'NAT traversal fix'. They denied any crypto policy changes, but could be lying.

Alice (support): Two parallel asks: Ben, can you force the gateway to re-establish with our old SA parameters and avoid rekey until we confirm? Ben: is there a quick mitigation like setting `rekey=no` on the tunnel?

Ben (netops): I can set `rekey=no` temporarily and restart the child SA; that'll prevent churn while we debug. Applying now.

infra-bot: Deploy job #8492: updated ipsec config on gw-rt0, set rekey=no for tunnel org-42 — success.

Ben (netops): Done. Tunnel shows stable, no more rekey attempts. Can you retest curl?

Carla (customer): Re-tested from pod: TLS handshake completes now and health returns 200. :thumbsup:

Dave (eng-runtime): Good. Now we need root cause: mismatch appears to be due to the third-party appliance preferring `aes_gcm8_128` (short tag) which we don't advertise by default. That caused the remote to pick an incompatible CHILD_SA proposal during rekey.

Ben (netops): I've extracted the IKE logs from their side (they shared): `CHILD_SA propose: AES_GCM_8_128/INTEGRITY_NONE/PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256` while our config disallows a 8-byte GCM tag for security policy.

Alice (support): For next steps: 1) Keep rekey disabled while we coordinate, 2) Ask vendor to rollback micro-update or match our proposals, 3) Plan safe rekey window with overlapping SA proposals.

Carla (customer): We're asking the appliance vendor to revert. They responded they're investigating and flagged a known issue.

Dave (eng-runtime): Also recommend we add an alert: repeated CHILD_SA rejection count > 3 for a tunnel => P0. Currently it was rolling under the radar because tunnel showed ESTABLISHED.

Ben (netops): Agree. Adding alert and a diagnostic automation to capture `ipsec statusall` + `tcpdump` for the next 10m on failure.

Alice (support): One more note: during the handshake failure the runtime also logged TLS servername mismatch because the control-plane connection fell back to IP (SAN mismatch). Keep an eye on cert rotate windows — if the control plane starts connecting by IP instead of DNS during flaps, TLS will fail even after tunnel recovers.

Carla (customer): Vendor reverted their update and re-applied with the old crypto profile. We're testing for 15m.

Carla (customer): Confirmed: traffic normal for 20m, no more 502s. Thanks.

Alice (support): Closing interim mitigation: rekey disabled. Next actions assigned: Ben will add alert and diag capture; Dave will add TLS/DNS fallback checks to the runtime; Carla will follow up with vendor postmortem.

Ben (netops): Note for postmortem: consider adding explicit matching proposals during initial tunnel setup to prevent vendor drift.

Dave (eng-runtime): Opened ticket RN-1274 to add CHILD_SA rejection alert and automate capture.

Carla (customer): Appreciated. We'll keep you posted if vendor gives root cause. :pray:

Alice (support): Thanks all — marking incident as resolved for now. Reopen if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
